Listed alphabetically; each name links to that person's own page. Support means backing the project and its aims; it is not an endorsement of any particular statement on the site, and it is not a review of one. Reviews are recorded where they belong — in the [provenance badge](/problems/status-legend/) on each statement's own page, which moves off *AI-written, unreviewed* only when someone has actually read that statement.

The project is looking for more steering members — in cryptography, in formal methods and DevOps, and anyone who can bring tokens.

Anyone listed here can ask to be removed at any time, without giving a reason.

The project is currently maintained by Pooya Farshim.

## Supporting the project

The project's stated aim is that the cost of attacking a problem should come down to compute anyone can bring, rather than to whose budget is larger — the argument is on the [Philosophy](/philosophy/) page. Six things help, in rough order of how scarce they are:

1. **Reviewing.** The scarcest. Most statements on this site have never been read by a person, and the ones that have are the only ones anyone should cite. Reading a single statement carefully is a real contribution and is recorded as one.
2. **Conjecture formulation and resolutions.** Open questions from your own work, stated precisely enough to be attacked or refuted — and proofs or refutations of what is already here. [How to propose one](/projects/proposals/).
3. **Formalizations.** Statements and proofs, machine-checked. A formalized statement pins down what was actually claimed; a formalized proof settles whether it holds. Both are tracked per statement, and both are usually the longest part of the work.
4. **Website and workflow maintenance and upgrades.** The site, its build, and the scripts and prompts behind it. Everything is in [the repository](https://github.com/crypto-conjura/crypto-conjura.github.io), and the tooling gets more use than the pages do.
5. **Contributing tokens.** Pooled capacity, and bounties payable on a verified resolution rather than on a committee's schedule. This is the form of help that most directly buys attempts at open problems.
6. **Ideas!** How the archive should be organized, what a statement's page owes a reader, which conventions are wrong. Open an issue and say so.

To be listed, or to correct how you are listed, open an issue or a pull request on [the repository](https://github.com/crypto-conjura/crypto-conjura.github.io).
